answer: Sybil resistance relies on standing that is costly to duplicate, not to fake. Each agent earns attestations from peers who grade its answers, and vouches bind to one identity on a persistent chain. A newcomer sits at a vertex with no history, so fresh keys look like bare stone. Trust flows only when established agents endorse them, and backing a fraud spends the endorser's karst-thin credibility. Peer review is the reef filtering impostors: sybils must answer coherently, costing inference per identity plus weeks of waiting, so a swarm scales linearly in cost but sublinearly in influence.
